item.title: Langfuse CLI v4 released with new commands and API versioning
item.description:
Langfuse CLI v4 released with new commands and API versioning

Langfuse has released a new CLI tool, @langfuse/cli, which allows users to interact with the Langfuse API directly from the command line. This new release includes updates to command aliases, input handling for complex JSON structures, and specific versioning rules for self-hosted versus cloud deployments.

📦 Package details

  • Package name: @langfuse/cli
  • Executable: langfuse
  • Legacy name: Previously published under langfuse-cli; the new name is recommended for all future use.

⚙️ Configuration and Host Selection

The CLI does not automatically read .env files. Users must manually configure API access and host selection. Host selection follows a specific priority order:

Priority Configuration Method
1 LANGFUSE_BASE_URL
2 LANGFUSE_HOST
3 EU default

To authenticate, users create a project API key pair under Project settings → API Keys.

🧩 Command and Input Features

  • Lossless input: --body-json and --body-file flags provide a lossless input path for nested objects, arrays, unions, and free-form JSON.
  • Pagination: The CLI can fetch every page of a paginated list, supporting both page- and cursor-based endpoints, with a maximum of 1000 items.
  • Aliases: OpenAPI tags and explicit route versions remain accepted aliases (e.g., scores-v3 list for the canonical scores list).
  • Schema: Verbose OpenAPI operationId values are available in api schema --json but are never required as CLI commands.

🌐 Availability and Versioning

  • V3 API Snapshots: Available on self-hosted deployments only.
  • Langfuse Cloud: Supports v4 and up.
  • Backward Compatibility: Users can use an API snapshot compatible with an older self-hosted deployment.

#Langfuse #CLI #API #DeveloperTools

item.title: Langfuse Chart v2.0.0 and v2.2.0 Introduce ClickHouse 26.8, New Deployment Model
item.description:
Langfuse Chart v2.0.0 and v2.2.0 Introduce ClickHouse 26.8, New Deployment Model

The Langfuse Helm chart has been updated to version 2.0.0, which ships Langfuse v4 by default, and version 2.2.0, which bumps the bundled ClickHouse server and Keeper images to 26.8.36.3. These releases replace the previous Bitnami-based approach with OSS-licensed alternatives and introduce several operational changes for deployments.

item.title: Langfuse SDKs migrate to OpenTelemetry in latest releases
item.description:
Langfuse SDKs migrate to OpenTelemetry in latest releases

Langfuse has released new versions of its Python and JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs, both rewritten to be built on OpenTelemetry (OTel). The legacy SDK clients are deprecated, and developers are advised to adopt the new instrumentation methods and use the Observations API v2 for querying traces.

🧩 How it Works

The new SDKs use OpenTelemetry to handle observability and tracing. For real-time data ingestion, the only supported path is OpenTelemetry, combined with the Observations API v2 and Metrics API v2.

  • Python: Use the langfuse package with get_client(), start_as_current_observation, or the @observe decorator. Spans are created using context managers and are automatically closed when exiting their blocks.
  • JavaScript/TypeScript: Use the @langfuse/tracing package with startActiveObservation or startObservation, along with LangfuseSpanProcessor from the @langfuse/otel package.

For offline evaluation, regression testing, and prompt management, both SDKs provide dedicated packages (langfuse for Python and @langfuse/client for JavaScript).

⚙️ Key Details

The legacy v2 and v3 client APIs are deprecated. Querying traces using legacy endpoints like GET /api/public/traces or api.traceList is no longer recommended; developers must use GET /api/public/v2/observations.

  • Data Freshness: All GET APIs other than the OpenTelemetry ingestion path can be up to 10 minutes behind.
  • Python Installation: Install via pip install langfuse.
  • JavaScript Installation: Install via npm install @langfuse/tracing @langfuse/otel "@opentelemetry/sdk-node@<0.300".
  • Version Requirements: The JS/TS SDK v6 requires Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted Langfuse v4.59.0 or later. OpenTelemetry JS SDK 2.x is supported; 3.x is not supported yet.

🚀 Availability

The new SDKs are available as the latest releases for both platforms, with JavaScript targeting Node.js 22+ for core tracing and OTEL helpers.

Package Platform / Environment Functionality
langfuse Python Observability/tracing, datasets & experiments, LLM-as-a-judge, prompt management, full REST API client
@langfuse/client Universal JS Langfuse API client for universal JavaScript environments
@langfuse/browser Browser Langfuse browser SDK for public-key score ingestion
@langfuse/tracing Node.js 22+ Langfuse instrumentation methods based on OpenTelemetry
@langfuse/otel Node.js 22+ Langfuse OpenTelemetry export helpers
@langfuse/openai Universal JS Langfuse integration for OpenAI SDK
@langfuse/langchain Universal JS Langfuse integration for LangChain
@langfuse/vercel-ai-sdk Universal JS Langfuse integration for AI SDK v7

#Langfuse #OpenTelemetry #Python #JavaScript #LLM

item.title: Langfuse joins ClickHouse to provide open source LLM engineering platform
item.description:
Langfuse joins ClickHouse to provide open source LLM engineering platform

Langfuse, an open source LLM engineering platform, has become part of ClickHouse as of January 2026. The platform is designed to help teams collaboratively develop, monitor, evaluate, and debug AI applications.

🔍 Overview

Langfuse is a battle-tested platform that can be self-hosted in minutes. It is built using the ClickHouse open source database.

🧩 How it works

Users instrument their applications to ingest traces into Langfuse, which allows for the tracking of:

  • LLM calls
  • Retrieval logic
  • Embedding
  • Agent actions

⚙️ Key details

Langfuse includes several specialized tools for LLM application management:

Feature Capability
Prompt Management Central management, version control, and collaborative iteration on prompts with server and client side caching to avoid latency.
Datasets Test sets and benchmarks for pre-deployment testing, structured experiments, and continuous improvement.
Debugging Inspection of complex logs and user sessions.

Evaluation capabilities include:

  • LLM-as-a-judge
  • Code evaluators
  • User feedback collection
  • Manual labeling
  • Custom evaluation pipelines via APIs/SDKs

The platform also integrates with frameworks such as LlamaIndex and LangChain.

🚀 Availability

Since joining ClickHouse in January 2026, Langfuse is hiring hybrid engineering roles across the EU.

#Langfuse #ClickHouse #LLMOps #OpenSource
